diagnosis.summary: The operator is launch-bound, not bandwidth-bound: 32x256 FP32 is 8192 elements (~32 KB) and the baseline's 6 kernel launches dominate the measured 14.336us (≈2.4us per launch). The only lever with real headroom is collapsing the whole elementwise chain into a single device-side launch via CUDA graph replay.
bottlenecks: Kernel-launch overhead dominates: baseline issues 6 launches (mul, mul, add, sub, relu, clone) for 8192 elements; per-launch cost ≈2.0-2.4us against ~14.3us total.
Eager launch gaps are visible to the timer; arithmetic itself is negligible for 32 KB of data.
candidate-02 was rejected by a pure Python UnboundLocalError before any kernel ran, so no graph-path evidence exists yet.

diagnosis.summary: The operator is launch-bound, not bandwidth-bound: 32x256 FP32 is 8192 elements (~32 KB) and the baseline's 6 kernel launches dominate the measured 14.336us (≈2.4us per launch). The only lever with real headroom is collapsing the whole elementwise chain into a single device-side launch via CUDA graph replay.
